title: A bridge, a boat, a lamp
hook: the friend who always does the airport run; Shantideva wishes to be a bridge, a boat, a lamp
carry: the bodhisattva's wish: to be the way across
tomorrow: how does a blind man find a jewel in the trash?

segments.voice: Yesterday: may I be a medicine. Shantideva wished to be medicine, doctor and nurse for everyone who's sick. May I be the medicine. Medicine was one wish. The list keeps going.
screen: `MAY I BE THE MEDICINE.` → `THE LIST KEEPS GOING.`

segments.voice: Every friend group has one. The person who does the airport run at five in the morning. Who explains the bus system to the new kid. Who leaves the porch light on when someone's coming home late. They rarely get thanked. They don't end up in the photos, because they're the ones holding the phone. They're just how everyone else gets where they're going. So, what else does Shantideva wish to be? Things exactly like that.
screen: `THE FIVE A.M. AIRPORT RUN.` → `THE PORCH LIGHT LEFT ON.` → `HOW EVERYONE ELSE GETS THERE.`

segments.voice: A few verses after the medicine, Shantideva's list grows. May I be a protector for those who have none, and a guide for travelers. For those who want to cross the water, may I be a boat, a bridge, a causeway. A lamp for anyone who needs light. A bed for anyone who needs rest. A servant for all who need one. Look at what's on that list. Not one of them is the destination. A bridge doesn't come along to the other side and ask for a seat at dinner. A boat drops you at the shore and goes back for the next person. A lamp lights the page; nobody reads the lamp. Every item is something used, and then left behind, without a thank-you. That's the point. The awakening mind he's been building since chapter one wants to be the way across for other people, not the place they arrive. And notice the size of it. You don't have to be a boat for everyone today. One crossing is still a crossing. One lamp is enough for one page. A bridge, a boat, a lamp.
screen: `A GUIDE, A BOAT, A BRIDGE.` · `A LAMP, A BED, A SERVANT.` · `NOT ONE IS THE DESTINATION.` · `ONE CROSSING IS STILL A CROSSING.` · then, large: `A BRIDGE, A BOAT, A LAMP.`

segments.voice: Think of one person who's stuck on some small crossing: a question, a lonely week, a hard first day. Write them a short text that helps them across, a tip, a link, a ride offered, or just a light left on. Read it once slowly, and send it now or when the sit ends.
A bridge: one of Shantideva's wishes, to be the way across for anyone who needs to cross, and then be left behind.
Your line: the bodhisattva's wish, to be the way across. A bridge, a boat, a lamp: nobody reads the lamp, and the page still gets read. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some Mahayana Buddhists recite this run of verses, may I be a protector, a guide, a boat, a bridge, a lamp, as part of daily practice, and some teachers ask students to choose one image to live by for a day.

fork.setup: a new coworker is lost in the company's systems and too shy to ask. you're busy. what fits Shantideva's list?

fork.reveal: a bridge gets someone across and stays behind. you don't carry her the whole way; you help her cross one gap.
